title: First flight
source: Charter first-flight.md: power on, connect through a gateway, Takeoff, Move To, Land, with the failure branch.

branches.failsafe: If the link drops during Move To (replaces the main steps after Move To starts)

steps.why: The drone opens the link through the gateway and says hello: its id, protocol version, its key and, this first time, the enrollment key. Reports and commands come next as admin.describe.
Core accepts the drone and confirms the version both sides will use.
After the hello is accepted, the drone describes itself: reports, commands and cameras. No keys. Core stores this and will forward it unchanged to operators.
Core stores the description and acknowledges it. Until it does, the drone resends the description and sends nothing else.
The drone reports its current settings, so Core knows what it will do if the link drops. This connect report lists every setting it supports.
Core acknowledges the connect report. Only now does the drone send its other reports.
The drone reports it is healthy and ready.
The drone reports where it is on the ground.
The drone reports its battery, on its own schedule.
Core sends Task T1: climb straight up to 30 m above its launch point. It sends each Task only after the drone has shown it holds the one before, so Tasks arrive in Core's order.
A Task was added, so the drone reports its queue. Core sees T1 arrived; had it not, Core would resend it.
T1 is listed, so Core sends Task T2: fly to a position, keeping the current altitude.
The drone reports its queue again. Core sees T2 arrived.
T2 is listed, so Core sends Task T3: go to 20 m, fly back over the landing spot and land.
The drone reports its queue. Core sees all 3 arrived, in its order.
The drone reports it started T1 (Takeoff).
The drone reports its climb.
The drone reports T1 done: it is holding at 30 m.
Core acknowledges the final report. Until it does, the drone resends T1's report unchanged; every final report gets this answer (not shown again below).
The drone reports it started T2 (Move To), the next Task in its queue.
The drone reports its position and speed on the way.
The drone reports its battery.
The drone reports T2 done: it is over the destination.
The drone reports it started T3 (Land), the last Task in its queue.
The drone reports it is back on the ground.
The drone reports T3 done. Its queue is now empty, so the run is over.
The drone reports its battery after landing.

Partway through Move To, the drone has heard nothing new from Core for 30 s (its link_loss_after_s), so it loses contact (the trigger) and returns to home (its link_loss_response setting). It sends this as soon as it can be heard again.
The drone reports T2 failed, so Core's record matches what happened.
The drone cancels the rest of its queue, so T3 (Land) is reported cancelled.
Clearing its queue also pauses the drone. A Task that arrives late waits until Core sets run_state running.
The drone reports its position on the way home.
The last Task finishing (an empty queue) marks the end of the run, but nothing covers the Reset ZIP yet. Not needed on the wire yet; listed so it is not forgotten.
